items.title: Presentation by M/s HIL (India) Limited, with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.27 of the 472nd Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding permission for liquidation of the stock-in-hand of HILNET (LLIN). The applicant appeared before the RC for making a presentation in terms of the RC decision taken in its 472nd meeting at agenda item no 10.36. The applicant has submitted that M/s HIL Ltd. is a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers and inter-alia engaged in the field of agrochemicals. The applicant is a holder of the Registration under section 9(3b) of LLIN with 0.667 % incorporated Alphacypermethrin. It was also submitted that they used to manufacture the LLIN at their manufacturing sites located at Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, MP, TN, WB, Odisha and Jharkhand. Applicant has further submitted that during the validity of their Certificate of Registration, they have manufactured a considerable quantity of LLIN and presently they have received verification report from the state of Tamil Nadu which were shown to the RC during presentation, which verify the quantity of raw material only not finished product. It was also informed by the concerned expert that as per records available no reports have been received by the Sectt. of CIB&RC from any State Govt. on the above issue. The RC observed from the presentation by the representatives of HIL that the stock statement reveals that there is no finished LLIN Product in the verified sites, it contains the quantity of raw material available at the inspected site. The applicant has informed that the verification report from other state authorities is awaited. The representatives were asked, whether they will need manufacturing license also to consume the raw material, which they responded in affirmative. RC is of the view that upon the receipt of the entire verification report from all the state authorities it would be in the proper state of affairs that RC should deliberated upon the entire material and thereof take a final decision in consonance of order issued by the DA&FW on the issue of extension of validity period and commercialization. RC therefore requested the applicant to submit the entire verification report from the respective state authorities so as to enable the RC to take a final view in the matter.
items.decision: The RC directed the Secretary (CIB&RC) to send a detailed communication to the DA&FW for seeking guidance as the present matter being a policy issue.

items.title: Presentation by M/s Ecoplants Co. Limited, with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.50 of the 472nd Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding technical presentation on 1-Methylcyclopropene(1-MCP) 12% Gas Generating.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 472nd RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 10.50), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation regarding the proposed registration of 1-Methylcyclopropene (1-MCP) 12% Gas Generating (GE) formulation. The representative of M/s Ecoplants Co. Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that the proposed product is a gas-generating formulation wherein the active ingredient, 1-Methylcyclopropene (1-MCP), is not manufactured, isolated or supplied as a conventional technical grade material. Instead, 1-MCP gas is generated in situ immediately prior to application by mixing two imported precursor components in a dedicated gas generator under controlled heating conditions, and the generated gas is directly released into sealed post-harvest chambers for use through a specially designed gas generator. The applicant submitted that, owing to this mode of generation, no standalone technical grade active ingredient exists in the conventional sense. It was further submitted that the product is intended exclusively for indoor post- harvest application in sealed chambers by trained personnel only, without direct exposure to soil, water or non-target organisms. Accordingly, the applicant requested the Registration Committee to frame an appropriate regulatory framework for registration of 1-MCP gas-generating systems and sought waiver of the technical and ecotoxicity data requirements on the ground that such data are not scientifically applicable to the proposed product. It was also informed that their product is already registered in various countries globally. After detailed deliberation, the Committee appreciated the utility of the proposed technology and accordingly, decided to constitute an expert group to examine the scientific and regulatory aspects of the proposal to recommend an appropriate regulatory framework for consideration. Further, the composition of the expert group as under: 1. Dr. K.L. Gurjar, JD (PP)-Chairman 2. Dr. Sonai Rajan, AD (Entomology)-Member 3. Dr. Swati Som, AD (Toxicology)-Member 4. Ms. Vineta Maheshwari, PPO (Chemistry)-Member Secretary

items.title: Presentation by M/s Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.43 of the 470th Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding for the registration of s-Metolachlor technical 96 % Min. u/s 9(3) TI.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 470th RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 10.43), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation to justify the adequacy of the submitted toxicological data in view of the use of test material with variable purity, the non-submission of a combined chronic toxicity/carcinogenicity study in rats, and the tumor findings observed in the submitted two-year rat oncogenicity study for the registration of s-Metolachlor technical 96 % Min. u/s 9(3) TI. The representative of M/s Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that S-Metolachlor is an enriched isomer of Metolachlor, requiring approximately 40% lower application rates than Metolachlor, thereby reducing operator exposure and environmental loading. The applicant submitted that a complete toxicological data package specific to S-Metolachlor has been generated and submitted in support of the application. It was further submitted that the bridging approach has been proposed only with respect to the chronic toxicity/carcinogenicity endpoint, based on the comparable metabolic profile and toxicological behavior of S-Metolachlor and Metolachlor. The applicant further stated that such scientific bridging has been accepted by regulatory authorities in several jurisdictions, including the USA, Canada, Brazil, Australia, Japan and the European Union, and referred to previous RC decisions wherein isomer-specific bridging was considered based on the overall weight of scientific evidence. The applicant further submitted that 12 of the 14 batches used in the toxicological studies met the minimum purity specification of 96%, while the remaining two batches had purity between 95% and 96%, with no batch below 95%. It was contended that the observed variation falls within the acceptable limits prescribed under the FAO specifications. The applicant also presented the proposed constitutive androstane receptor (CAR)-mediated mode of action for liver tumor formation in rats and submitted that the observed hepatocellular tumors are rodent-specific and not relevant to humans. After detailed deliberation, the Committee accepted the applicant's scientific justification regarding the purity variation of the test material used in the toxicological studies. The Committee noted that S-Metolachlor continues to be registered in several major jurisdictions, including the USA, Canada, Japan and Brazil. However, it also noted that the approval of S-Metolachlor was not renewed in the European Union from 2024 due to concerns, inter alia, relating to groundwater contamination and unresolved issues of mutagenicity and carcinogenicity. Accordingly, the Committee directed the applicant to submit adequate scientific evidence addressing the human relevance of the proposed CAR- mediated mode of action, the carcinogenicity concerns, and measures to mitigate groundwater contamination. The Committee further clarified that bridging of toxicological data for isomeric active ingredients shall be considered only on a case-to-case basis based on the totality of scientific evidence and a weight-of-evidence approach, and shall not constitute a general precedent. The matter shall be considered further upon submission and evaluation of the requisite information by the applicant.

items.title: Presentation by M/s Deccan Fine Chemicals (India) Pvt. Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 10.27 of the 473rd Registration Committee (RC) Meeting regarding for representation of application of Florpyrauxifen Benzyl technical 94.0 % w/w Min. u/s 9(3) TIM vs TI.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 473rd RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 10.27), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation regarding the proposal for registration of Florpyrauxifen-benzyl Technical 94.0% w/w Min. under Section 9(3) TIM vs TI, of the Insecticides Act, 1968 wherein the equivalence has been claimed with M/s Corteva Crop India Pvt. Ltd. u/s 9(3) TI with a minimum purity of 92.0% w/w. The representative of M/s Deccan Fine Chemicals Pvt. Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that the proposed indigenous technical has been developed through technology transfer from M/s Corteva Agriscience LLC under the Make in India initiative, with an improved manufacturing process resulting in an increase in the minimum purity from 92.0% w/w to 94.0% w/w. They further stated that this site shall be supplying this product to M/s Corteva Agriscience LLC for global supply. The technology of manufacturing Florpyrauxifen – benzyl (Rinskor™) technical is developed by M/s. Corteva Crop India Pvt Ltd. The same technology has been transferred to M/s. Deccan Fine Chem Pvt. Ltd. For global supply including India too. The application is complete from Bio-efficacy and Legal divisions, and currently under scrutiny from Toxicology, Chemistry and Packaging divisions. Deccan has submitted replies to Chemistry and Toxicology divisions which are under scrutiny. The current application was discussed in the 473rd meeting of the Registration Committee (RC), vide agenda item 10.27, held on 29.06.2026. The RC decided to call the applicant for presentation. The representatives of the applicant submitted that 94% purity technical manufactured through new route is registered in 68 countries and M/s. Deccan obtained registration for export of 94% pure Rinskor™ technical which is used globally, other than India. They further explained that The US EPA uses the “Test guidelines for pesticides and toxic substances*” Code Federal Regulations 40CFR158 to assess that the active ingredient doesn’t introduce new toxicological or environmental risks. The EU equivalency process follows the “Plant Protection Products Regulation 1107/2009” and uses a two-tiered approach (SANCO-10597/2003): 1. Tier I: Focuses on chemical profiles (identity, analytical profiles of 5- batch analysis, and impurity profiles). 2. Tier II: If Tier I cannot establish equivalency, Tier II requires mammalian toxicity and ecotoxicity testing to determine whether any new impurities increase the overall hazard to health or the environment. 3. Both approaches have been used to demonstrate the equivalency of Florpyrauxifen benzyl from the Deccan source to the US source. The Deccan source has been approved in both the US and EU. Both approaches are compliant with the equivalence assessment method outlined in the “Manual on development and use of FAO and WHO specifications for Pesticides” (2025) The applicant presented the outcome of the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier 1", wherein it was submitted that the Tier 1 criteria, namely: a) The certified minimum purity is not lower than that of the reference source; b) No new impurities are present; c) The limits of relevant impurities, as certified for the reference source, are not increased; and d) The certified limits of all non-relevant impurities are not increased beyond the acceptable limits. The applicant further presented the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier 1 Toxicological Results" and explained that the increase in the certified minimum purity from 92% to 94% w/w and the observed increase in the impurity were evaluated and found acceptable. The applicant further presented the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier 2" and the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Tier-II Toxicological Results". It was submitted that the proposed source was evaluated through the recommended Tier 2 toxicological studies, including the acute toxicity six-pack and genotoxicity studies, and that the results demonstrated that the Florpyrauxifen-benzyl Technical manufactured by the applicant is toxicologically equivalent to the reference source. The applicant also presented the "Chemical Equivalence Assessment Process – Overall Toxicological Results", wherein all relevant impurities were evaluated and concluded to be acceptable under the Tier II FAO equivalence assessment, with no toxicologically relevant impurities identified and no increase in hazard observed. The applicant presented that the registered TI of the same product contains 12 numbers of impurities. The applicant has removed nine number of impurities (including others impurities containing unidentified impurities <0.1 wt%) and two numbers of impurities have been reduced in quantification. Eight number of new impurities have been added/generated in the CC of the present applicant. The applicant further submitted that as per the requirement of 449th meeting, if chemical equivalence is not established, they have submitted additional data to fulfill the regulatory and safety requirement. The Committee observed that the applicant has addressed the requirements of the guidelines approved by the Registration Committee in its 449th meeting regarding assessment of chemical equivalence. The applicant submitted that although an increase in impurity levels was observed due to the improved manufacturing process, in accordance with the provisions of the 449th RC guidelines, which states that: “If impurities are identified, quantified and are not within limits of registered technical or if impurities are not within ±3%) and/or any additional impurity is present then in addition to the tests as indicated in (4) above, additional tests based on the nature and quantity of impurity and QSAR alert will be taken on case-to-case basis.” Therefore, the RC feels that the proposal is in compliance with the 449th RC guidelines on chemical equivalence assessment. The Committee further acknowledged that the implementation of solvent recycling systems in the proposed manufacturing process, leading to a lowered Process Mass Intensity (PMI), decreased raw solvent consumption, reduced metal catalyst dependencies, minimized waste generation, and significant net savings in global warming potential and carbon intensity. The Committee also noted the supporting data submitted for the new Florpyrauxifen-benzyl source specification in key geographies, including the USA, European Union, Australia and Japan, and the applicant's submission that the new source has been accepted by the respective regulatory authorities. After detailed deliberation, the Registration Committee found the chemistry- related justification, chemical equivalence assessment under Tier 1 and Tier 2, toxicological evaluation, manufacturing process improvements and supporting data to be satisfactory and agreed with the proposal for Florpyrauxifen-benzyl Technical 94.0% w/w Min. under Section 9(3) TIM vs TI. The application shall be put up to RC as and when complete in compliance of above decision.

items.title: Presentation by M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 6.55 of the 471st RC Meeting regarding registration of indigenous manufacture of Carfentrazone ethyl Technical 90% w/w Min. under section 9(3) TIM vs TI.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 473rd RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 6.55), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation to justify the non-submission of mutagenicity data required for registration of Carfentrazone- ethyl Technical 90% w/w Min. under Section 9(3) TIM vs TI. The representative of M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that the application was filed on 06.03.2023, and that, as per the then applicable guideline mutagenicity data were not required where the chemical composition is identical to that of the registered Section 9(3) technical. The applicant further submitted that chemical equivalence with the registered Section 9(3) technical had been established and, accordingly, mutagenicity data were not generated. In support of its submission, the applicant referred to the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.26) and submitted that the said decision specifically addressed mutagenicity requirements in relation to chemical equivalence. The applicant also referred to the decisions of the 442nd and 443rd RC Meetings, submitting that the implementation date of the revised Toxicology Guidelines had not been finalized and, therefore, the application should be considered under the applicable guidelines in force at the time of submission. After detailed deliberation, the Committee observed that the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.26) relied upon by the applicant pertained specifically to applications under Section 9(4) TIM and was not applicable to applications under Section 9(3). The Committee was of the view that submission of mutagenicity data is essential for the scientific evaluation of the technical grade active ingredient and for ensuring its safety. Accordingly, the Committee directed the applicant to submit the complete mutagenicity data package in accordance with the applicable Toxicology Guidance Document, including the Ames test and the requisite in vitro and in vivo genotoxicity studies, for further consideration of the application. After detailed deliberation, the Committee observed that the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.26) relied upon by the applicant pertained specifically to applications under Section 9(4) TIM and was not applicable to the present application under Section 9(3). The Committee further observed that the regulatory framework governing the present application, including the Guidance Document on Toxicology for Registration of Chemical Pesticides adopted by the RC in its 376th Meeting and finalized in its 377th Meeting, read together with the guidelines approved by the RC in its 381st, 440th, 442nd and 449th Meetings, requires submission of the mutagenicity data package as an essential component of the toxicological data requirements for the scientific evaluation and safety assessment of technical grade active ingredients. The Committee noted that such data are fundamental for the assessment of the genotoxic potential of the technical grade active ingredient and are indispensable for arriving at a scientifically sound and regulatory-compliant decision regarding its safety. Accordingly, the Committee decided that the applicant shall submit the complete mutagenicity data package as prescribed under the Guidance Document on Toxicology for Registration of Chemical Pesticides, for further scientific evaluation and consideration of the application.

items.title: Presentation by M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd., with reference to Agenda Item No. 6.62 of the 471st RC Meeting regarding registration of Picoxystrobin 10% + Copper Oxy Chloride 35% WG u/s 9(3) FIM.
items.decision: RC recalled its decision taken in the 471st RC Meeting (Agenda Item No. 6.62), wherein the applicant was invited to make a detailed presentation to justify higher acute oral toxicity of the formulation than that of the individual technical active ingredients for grant of registration U/s 9(3) FIM. The representative of M/s Crystal Crop Protection Ltd. made a presentation before the Committee and submitted that although the proposed formulation exhibited higher acute oral toxicity (LD₅₀ >300 to ≤2000 mg/kg body weight; GHS Category 4) than the individual technical active ingredients, it falls under the Blue Toxicity Triangle category and does not represent the highly hazardous toxicity classes. The applicant further submitted that the acute dermal toxicity (LD₅₀ >2000 mg/kg body weight) was comparable to both technical active ingredients, while the acute inhalation toxicity (LC₅₀ >4.32 mg/L) was lower than that of Picoxystrobin Technical (>2.12 mg/L) and Copper Oxychloride Technical (2.83 mg/L). The applicant also submitted that the formulation was non-irritant to skin and eyes, whereas the individual technical active ingredients were reported as slight irritants to irritants, and was non-sensitizing, similar to both technical active ingredients. Accordingly, the applicant submitted that the observed increase in acute oral toxicity did not alter the overall hazard classification of the formulation. After detailed deliberation, the Committee found the applicant's scientific justification regarding the higher acute oral toxicity of the proposed formulation to be satisfactory and agreed that the application may be processed further in accordance with the applicable regulatory provisions.

items.title: Consideration of the Report of the Expert Committee on the restricted Use of Glyphosate. At the outset, RC observes that DA&FW is reviewing the issue of the Glyphosate in terms of the directions given by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court and the issue is sub-judice. Presently an expert group has been constituted by PPA to conduct a scientific evaluation and examination of all the new evidence/recent submissions made by the Pesticides Associations inter-alia on the issue of the use of Glyphosate.
items.decision: RC perused the report submitted by the Expert group and after detailed scientific deliberations, also recalls that the issue has been dealt by the RC in its various past meetings which are the matter of records. RC is of the considered view that in view of the precautionary principle governing the issue, the use of Glyphosate is required to be restricted through PCO’s and the RC could not find any cogent scientific justifications for continued use of Glyphosate without any restrictions. RC therefore decided that the use of Glyphosate should be restricted and the same may be carried out through trained personnel’s/ PCOs to avoid any risk of occupational hazards and to prevent its misuse. RC directs the Secretary of CIB&RC to communicate this decision to DA&FW for taking an appropriate final view in the matter.

items.title: Gazette Notification dated 08.07.2026 issued by the Central Govt amending the Insecticides Rules 1971 mandating the requirement of an import permit for non- insecticidal uses.
items.decision: RC perused the Gazette Notification dated 08.07.2026 issued by the Central Govt (DA&FW) amending the Insecticides Rules 1971 called as the Insecticides Third Amendment Rules 2026 stipulating the requirement of an import permit for non- insecticidal uses. RC observed that the notification is statutory in nature and has a force of Law and therefore is required to be adhered by all the applicants desiring to import any of the substance included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act, 1968, for non-insecticidal purposes. RC therefore in supersession of all its earlier decision on the subject of import permit decided to comply with the notification dated 08.07.2026. RC also observed that the said notification includes the Form in which an application for grant of permission for import of insecticides for non-insecticidal use is to be made. RC decided that henceforth all the applications are to be made in the stipulated Form and the said notification is required to be put in public domain for information and compliance of all the stakeholders immediately. The finalized guidelines and Form are attached as Annexure-3.2.1. It was further decided that the applications of import permit pending in the Sectt. of CIB&RC shall also be dealt in accordance with revised guidelines with the then application form. RC also directs the Secretariate of CIB&RC to issue a public notice to this effect along with an appropriate guideline, forms approved by the RC as notified. A communication shall also be issued to the Custom Authorities for their information and compliance. RC also perused the communication received from M/s Supreme Petrochem Ltd. dated 24.07.2026 regarding the applicability of the Hon’ble Gujarat High Court Order dated 19.11.2025 wherein the requirement of import permit has been set aside to the extent of acrylonitrile to be imported for non-insecticidal use. RC deliberated upon the same and observes that since now the import permit requirement has been stipulated in the Insecticide Rules, 1971 by the way of the Gazette notification dated 08.07.2026 and therefore the requirement of obtaining an import permit is now a statutory requirement and therefore is required to be complied by all applicants for any of the substances proposed to be imported for non-insecticidal uses including acrylonitrile. Secretariat of CIB&RC is directed to communicate M/s Supreme Petrochem Ltd accordingly. RC feels expedient that this decision may also be communicated to DGFT, the regulatory authority vested with the powers of framing the policy pertaining the imports/exports under Ministry of Commerce under the Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act, 1992 for information and further needful in the matter.

items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda and decided as per Annexure –8.1.1 In case of satisfactory cases, CRs shall be issued only after KYC compliance of the applicant account and submission of the original affidavit, as per the format provided in 439th RC, by the applicant, duly forwarded by the authorized signatory only, within 15 days from the uploading of the minutes. In case the original affidavit is already submitted, then the applicant is required to email the copy of the acknowledgement, within 15 days from the uploading of the minutes to reconcile, afterwards, no such request shall be entertained to issue the CR. It was also directed to strictly follow Gazette Notification SO 3951 (E) dated 08.08.2018 published on 09.08.2018 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, while issuing approvals.

items.title: Clarification regarding exemption for requirement of Import Permit for import of Certified Reference Materials (CRMs)-in continuation to Agenda Item No. 10.9 of the Minutes of the 473rd Meeting of the Registration Committee (RC). In Agenda Item 10.9 of the Minutes of the 473rdRC, the restriction on "commercial use, formulation, manufacturing, sale, distribution or field application" is intended to ensure that Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) which may include banned and/or restricted pesticides and laboratory reagents that are included in the schedule of the Insecticides Act, 1968 are not diverted for sale and use as pesticide products. The statement is not intended to restrict their supply through traders and distributors. Since, Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) and laboratory reagents are predominantly imported and supplied to the end- users through traders and distributors, extending the exemption to traders and distributors ensures uninterrupted supply of CRMs and laboratory reagents for analytical, testing, calibration, quality assurance, and research purposes only. A public notice shall be issued on the website for the general awareness of all stakeholders.

items.title: Clarification required for the application submitted by M/s Saraswati Agro Chemicals (India).
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda regarding the application of M/s Saraswati Agro Chemicals (India) Pvt. Ltd. for registration of Formetanate Hydrochloride 20% SP (Formetanate Hydrochloride 23.3% w/w) for formulation indigenous manufacture under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968. The Committee noted that the toxicity studies submitted in support of the proposed formulation had been conducted using test materials differing in active ingredient concentration, study period, sponsors, test facilities and batches. In particular, the active ingredient concentration of the test materials ranged from approximately 10% to 93%, which does not correspond to the proposed formulation containing 23.3% w/w Formetanate Hydrochloride and is not consistent with the principles of toxicological equivalence under the FAO/WHO Manual on Development and Use of Pesticide Specifications and the applicable Indian regulatory framework. The Committee further observed that the Certificates of Analysis and supporting documents submitted were insufficient to establish the identity and equivalence of the tested materials with the proposed formulation. It was also noted that the acute oral toxicity study was not conducted in accordance with the applicable OECD Test Guideline, the acute dermal toxicity study had been conducted on the technical material instead of the proposed formulation, and adequate documentary evidence authorizing reliance on studies generated by different sponsors had not been furnished. In the absence of adequate scientific justification and supporting evidence establishing the equivalence of the tested materials with the proposed formulation, the Committee observed that the submitted toxicological data package does not adequately establish the safety profile of the proposed formulation. Accordingly, the Committee decided that the applicant be invited to make a detailed presentation before the RC in the next meeting to justify the scientific validity and regulatory acceptability of the submitted toxicological data.

items.title: Consideration of Request for technical presentation by M/s. Trical soil Solutions India Pvt. Ltd. regarding Chloropicrin.
items.decision: RC noted the request of M/s Trical Soil Solutions India Pvt. Ltd. seeking an opportunity to make a technical presentation regarding Chloropicrin. After detailed deliberation, and in line with its earlier decision, the Committee observed that Chloropicrin is an intrinsically highly hazardous soil fumigant and a highly volatile compound with severe acute toxicity. The Committee noted that Chloropicrin is a potent irritant to the eyes, skin and respiratory tract, capable of causing severe pulmonary injury, including chemical pneumonitis and delayed pulmonary oedema following inhalation exposure. The Committee further observed that repeated exposure may result in chronic respiratory impairment and systemic toxicity affecting vital organs. The Committee also noted its historical use as a chemical warfare agent and that, owing to its hazardous toxicological profile, its use in countries where it is permitted is subject to stringent regulatory restrictions, including strict occupational exposure limits and risk mitigation measures. Accordingly, the Committee did not agree to the request for a technical presentation and reiterated that the hazards associated with Chloropicrin decisively outweigh its potential benefits and, therefore, its registration is not warranted in India. 10.34 Decision taken by the registration committee at agenda item no. 10.7 in the 453 RC meeting regarding closure of user accounts and shifting to freezed category for non-replying to deficiency raised for more than two months in the KYC module. Registration Committee perused the requests received from applicants as per Annexure-10.34.1 for unfreezing of their user accounts deactivated as per the decision taken vide agenda item No. 10.7 of 453 RC meeting due to non- submission of deficiency reply for more than two months in the KYC module and decided that all the stakeholders whose user accounts have been deactivated/freezed due to the decision taken vide agenda item No. 10.7 of 453 RC meeting due to non-submission of deficiency reply for more than two months in the KYC module shall be given a one-time opportunity to submit the deficiency reply for completion of KYC. Accordingly, all such applicants are directed to submit request for unfreezing their user accounts with complete justification to the Secretary CIB&RC within one month from the date of publication of these minutes. The same shall be presented to the RC in its next meeting for appropriate decision. It was also further decided that all such accounts for which no request for unfreezing are received within 30 days shall be permanently closed and no further request shall be entertained.

Whereas the draft rules further to amend the Insecticides Rules, 1971, was published, as required by section 36 of the Insecticides Act, 1968 (46 of 1968), vide notification of the Government of India in the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare) number G.S.R. 855 (E), dated the 18th November, 2025, and published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i), dated the 19th November, 2025, inviting objections and suggestions from all persons likely to be affected thereby, before the expiry of a period of thirty days from the date on which the copies of the Official Gazette in which the said notification was published, were made available to the public; And whereas, copies of the said notification were made available to the public on 19th day of November, 2025; And whereas, objections or suggestions received from the public in respect of the said draft rules have been considered by the Central Government; Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by section 36 of the said Act, the Central Government hereby makes the following rules further to amend the Insecticides Rules, 1971, namely:- 1. Short title and Commencement.- (1) These rules may be called the Insecticides Third (Amendment) Rules, 2026. (2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 2. In the Insecticides Rules, 1971 (hereinafter referred to as the said rules), in rule 4, after clause (b), the following clause shall be inserted, namely:- (6) - (4) 4-6 - [ II 3(i)] 3. In the said rules, after Chapter III, the following Chapter shall be inserted, namely:- MANNER OF IMPORT OF AN INSECTICIDE FOR NON-INSECTICIDAL PURPOSE 8A. Manner of import.- (1) An application for import of an insecticide for non-insecticidal purpose shall be made to the Registration Committee in Form IA. (2) The application under sub-rule (1) shall be accompanied by a fee of rupees five thousand only. (3) The Registration Committee shall have the power to conduct an enquiry to verify the information furnished by the applicant. (4) An application which is complete in all respect shall be considered and disposed by the Registration Committee preferably within a period of forty-five days which may further extend to a period not later than fifteen days. (5) The import permit granted under sub-rule (4) shall be valid for one year. (6) If an applicant holds a certificate of registration for the pesticide for which the imported goods are intended to be 4.
